title: Hopper FP8 inference fingerprint guards and calibration pipeline ops
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Summary: Enable a conservative, observable FP8 path on Hopper (E4M3/E5M2) backed by an inference 'fingerprint' and operator-level guards. This ticket coordinates the calibration workflow, runtime heuristics for per-request fallback to INT8/FP16, and the acceptance criteria for safe rollout in hosted and Dedicated clusters.

Background: Our experiments show FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) can reduce token cost and memory pressure, but several instability modes appear at runtime for certain models and sequence-length distributions. Instead of a blind global activation, we need a layered approach: dataset-aware calibration, per-model/operator fingerprints, and a lightweight runtime guard that rejects or downgrades requests when fidelity or numerical stability risks are detected.

Goals:
- Implement an "inference fingerprint" computed during calibration runs (per-model, per-seq-length bucket) capturing operator scale distributions, max-clipped-values, and KV cache statistics.
- Wire a calibration pipeline that emits fingerprint artifacts and a signed threshold profile for E4M3 and E5M2.
- Runtime: add a guard that compares live request fingerprints to golden profiles and performs a deterministic fallback to INT8/FP16 when divergences exceed thresholds.
- Observability: surface divergence metrics, per-model fallback rate, and a regression alert tied to the quality harness.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration pipeline produces stable fingerprints for at least 90% of model+seq-buckets in the golden suite.
- Runtime fallback rate across canary customers < 3% and quality regressions (perplexity/ROUGE delta on canonical prompts) < 1% vs baseline FP16.
- Playbook and automated rollback are validated in a shadow canary and one controlled customer Dedicated cluster.

Implementation plan:
1) Calibration: extend existing calibrator to compute fingerprint vector (operator-scale histogram, outlier count, per-layer dynamic range) and store JSON artifact to GCS and Confluence link.
2) Threshold derivation: offline job that picks conservative thresholds per operator and sequence-length bucket (configurable, versioned).
3) Runtime: lightweight comparator in serving path that loads profile metadata and evaluates a fast fingerprint from the first micro-batch. If divergence, mark request for fallback.
4) Telemetry: emit fingerprint-match-status, fallback-reason, and numeric deltas; add dashboard in Console with per-model breakdown.
5) Rollout: shadow-mode -> limited canary -> tenant promote with automated rollback if quality or SLOs degrade.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Chose a conservative fingerprint (statistical summaries rather than full histograms) to keep runtime overhead <1% latency.
- Fallback to INT8 first where available, else FP16. This balances cost savings and safety.
- We will not attempt per-token dynamic quantization on first rollout due to complexity; keep that for a follow-up.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/QPROTO/FP8+Inference+Fingerprint (draft)
- Design spec (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1FP8FingerprintSpec
- Calibration job PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibrator/pull/892
- Runtime guard PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1503
- Canary dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/fp8-fallback-canary

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: fingerprint false positives causing excessive fallbacks -> mitigate by conservative thresholds and a staged canary with telemetry gating.
- Risk: calibration drift over time -> mitigation: schedule weekly recalibration for high-traffic models and snapshot baselines for regressions.
- Risk: correlation between fingerprint divergence and downstream quality unknown for some edge models -> include small-sample human eval in canary.
